item.title: Proposed social media ban aims to protect children - Tabuya
item.description: The proposed ban on social media for children aged 16 and under marks an important step in protecting our children and promoting the responsible use of social media. Minister for Information, Environment and Climate Change Lynda Tabuya shared this with the children at Villa Four Settlement, Nasinu.
item.content:encoded:
The proposed ban on social media for children aged 16 and under marks an important step in protecting our children and promoting the responsible use of social media.

Minister for Information, Environment and Climate Change Lynda Tabuya shared this with the children at Villa Four Settlement, Nasinu.

Tabuya says the views gathered from the forum will contribute to a report being prepared by the task force, chaired by her ministry together with the Ministry of Communications.

The Minister says the report will then be presented to Cabinet, along with draft legislation proposing a ban on social media access for children aged 16 and under.

item.title: Three more arrested over alleged aggravated robbery in Nabua
item.description: Three more men have been arrested following another raid by the Southern Division Task Force in connection with an alleged aggravated robbery at Sukanaivalu Road in Nabua yesterday. Police say the three men, aged 27, 23 and 21, were arrested during an afternoon raid.
item.content:encoded:
Three more men have been arrested following another raid by the Southern Division Task Force in connection with an alleged aggravated robbery at Sukanaivalu Road in Nabua yesterday.

Police say the three men, aged 27, 23 and 21, were arrested during an afternoon raid.

This brings the total number of arrests to four, after a man in his 20s was arrested at Sukanaivalu Road earlier in the day.

Police say the four men allegedly hired the victim’s taxi from Narere to Nabua and, after arriving at their destination, stole the driver’s watch and cash.

item.title: National Agriculture Show returns to Labasa after six-years, farmers to learn new farming methods
item.description: After a six-year break, the National Agriculture Show is returning to Labasa, with farmers set to learn about new farming technologies, food security, income generation and ways to deal with the prolonged dry spell. The three-day event will be held from tomorrow to Thursday at Subrail Park , using Ground 1 and Ground 2.
item.content:encoded:
After a six-year break, the National Agriculture Show is returning to Labasa, with farmers set to learn about new farming technologies, food security, income generation and ways to deal with the prolonged dry spell.

The three-day event will be held from tomorrow to Thursday at Subrail Park , using Ground 1 and Ground 2.

Speaking to fijivillage News, Divisional Agriculture Officer North Sujendra Prasad highlighted that new technologies and farming methods will be introduced to help farmers deal with current challenges, including the fuel crisis and the prolonged drought spell.

Singh says farmers will be shown ways to improve food production and generate income, with practical knowledge they can take back and use on their farms.

He says breeding animals will be brought from Viti Levu, including cattle, sheep, goats and pigs, and will be displayed during the event.

He says information booths will also provide farmers, agriculture students and members of the public with pamphlets, leaflets and posters containing useful farming information.

item.title: Ganesh Utsav begins as devotees seek blessings for wisdom and prosperity
item.description: Ganesh Utsav, a 10-day Hindu festival celebrating the birth of Lord Ganesha, begins today with devotees coming together in prayer to seek blessings for wisdom, prosperity, good fortune and new beginnings. Lord Ganesha is revered as the remover of obstacles, and the festival traditionally begins with Ganpati Sthapana, where an idol of Lord Ganesha is installed.
item.content:encoded:
Ganesh Utsav, a 10-day Hindu festival celebrating the birth of Lord Ganesha, begins today with devotees coming together in prayer to seek blessings for wisdom, prosperity, good fortune and new beginnings.

Lord Ganesha is revered as the remover of obstacles, and the festival traditionally begins with Ganpati Sthapana, where an idol of Lord Ganesha is installed.

Devotees perform prayers and aarti and make offerings including flowers, incense, diyas, fruits and sweets, particularly modak.

Families also welcome Lord Ganesha, affectionately known as Bappa, into their homes, while communities hold devotional and cultural programmes during the celebrations.

The festival concludes with Ganesh Visarjan, which is the immersion of Lord Ganesha’s idol in water.

Meanwhile, the Sanatan Shiv Mandir in Samabula will begin its Ganesh Utsav celebrations with the Ganapati Murti Sthapna at 7 tonight.

The Shree Ganesh Puran Katha will be held from tomorrow to next Thursday at 7pm each day.

The Mandir says devotees, families and members of the wider Sanatan community are welcome to visit and offer prayers to Lord Ganesha from today until next Friday.
